name: Adventist movement (Millerites)

citations.excerpt: The sects of Adventists are the outcome of a religious agitation begun by William Miller (1781-1849) in 1831, after a minute study of the prophecies of the Bible .

facts.value: Belief in the near, personal return of Christ.

citations.excerpt: hold in common a belief in the near return of Christ in person

facts.value: Miller predicted Christ's return in 1843, and a follower revised it to 22 October 1844. After the expected date passed, followers met at Albany in 1845 and the movement divided into several bodies.

citations.excerpt: Snow, one of his disciples, set himself to correct Miller's calculations, and in his turn announced the end of the world for 22 October, 1844.
The faithful followers of Miller next met in conference at Albany , N.Y., in 1845
Miller concluded that the world would come to an end, and Christ would return, in A.D. 1843.

research_notes: Miller was a Baptist; candidate parent Baptists kept as lane parent but no split_from fact sourced.
